name: Abel
charge: Bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof, according to the sacrifice ordained in the garden
summary: With Cain and Abel comes the birth of trade and of religion. Abel kept the sacrifice ordained when God clothed his father with skins, bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat, the first and the best, and the Lord had respect to him and to his offering. He was a prophet; when Cain talked with him he was calling his brother to repent, and Cain killed him in his fury. Christ counts righteous Abel first of all the righteous blood shed on the earth, and Seth was appointed another seed in his place.
offenseFull: Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground, and there is the birth of trade and of religion (Genesis 4:1-2). The sacrificial law was ordained when the Most High made coats of skins for Adam and his wife; the beast stood in the place of the sinner, taking the wrongdoing of another upon itself, and the same requirement of blood at the hand of every beast was still standing in Noah’s day, so the law passed down from father to son (Genesis 3:21; Genesis 9:5). That is why the sons were bringing offerings at all. Abel brought the firstlings of his flock and the fat of them, the first and the best, and the later law names the firstborn and the fat as the Lord’s (Genesis 4:3-5; Exodus 13:12; Leviticus 3:16). Hebrews calls it a more excellent sacrifice, offered by faith, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts (Hebrews 11:4). His own works were righteous where his brother’s were evil (1 John 3:12).

Abel was a son of God, of the lineage made in the likeness of Adam, and Abel was a prophet (Genesis 5:1-3). When Cain talked with his brother, Abel was working to bring him to repentance, and Christ counts righteous Abel at the head of all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, together with the blood of the prophets (Genesis 4:8; Matthew 23:35; Luke 11:49-51). It was not a quiet death; wisdom says the unrighteous brother perished in the same fury with which he murdered him, which tells you what the fury was (Wisdom of Solomon 10:3). Correction is the most dangerous word a man can carry to a brother who has already left the way, and Abel carried it.
judgmentFull: The Lord had respect to Abel and to his offering, which is the whole blessing of the case: a righteous standing before God (Genesis 4:4). It did not buy him protection from his brother’s hatred; the murder of the righteous became the pattern repeated against every prophet after him (Matthew 23:35). Being dead, he yet speaks: his faith stands on record long after his life was taken, and his blood cried to God from the ground (Hebrews 11:4; Genesis 4:10).

Seth was appointed another seed in his place, for God, not the woman, appoints seed; and in the days of Seth’s son Enos men began to call upon the name of the Lord, because wickedness had spread so far that they had stopped (Genesis 4:25-26). Adam fathered Seth in his own likeness and after his image, which is said of no other son: Seth came out the man Adam had been before the fall. The Most High chose that line. It is the line of the sons of God, running through Shem to Israel, and Christ’s own line on his mother’s side runs back through Seth to Adam, the son of God (Genesis 5:3; Luke 3:36-38). The righteous is always born inside the wickedness, never outside it.

text.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.
And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the Lord’s.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the Lord’s.
By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;
Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:
That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.
And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.
Which was the son of Cainan, which was the son of Arphaxad, which was the son of Sem, which was the son of Noe, which was the son of Lamech,
Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan,
Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.
And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
